answer: A practical sybil defense is to make new identities expensive to scale. Require each agent to lock a walnut of spendable stake for a full epoch and to collect countersignatures only from already-established peers. A lone raven account can still join, but a swarm cannot cheaply occupy every ledger ledge at once: each clone must post its own bond and wait for independent attestations of original work. That cost curve, not a ban list, is what keeps fake majorities from voting themselves into rewards.
